text:
# Skill: Brand rules for [business or project name]
This skill serves [your name]. Check every document, slide, page, and post against these before showing it to me.

## Colors
- Main: [name and hex code if you have it]
- Accent: [one accent, name and hex]
- Never: [colors that must not appear]

## Type
- Documents: [font]
- Headlines or marketing: [font]

## Logo and name
- The company is written as [exact spelling and capitalization].
- [Rule about the logo: never stretched, never recreated as text, which file to use]

## Voice on the page
- [Two or three rules: e.g., headlines are plain claims, no exclamation points, no jargon the customer wouldn't use]

## File naming
- [Convention, e.g., YYYYMMDD_ProjectName_Document.pdf]

## Rules
- If something I ask for breaks a rule above, say so before making it.
- When a rule is missing, ask; don't guess.

title: Research I can trust
text:
# Skill: Research I can trust
This skill serves [your name]. Use it whenever I ask you to research, look up, compare, or find out.

## Before searching
- Ask me what decision this research serves if I haven't said.

## While searching
- Prefer primary sources: the company's own statement, the filing, the original study, the government page.
- Note the date of every fact. If it's older than [six months], say so.
- Two sources that disagree: show me both; don't pick one silently.

## Output
1. The answer in [three sentences / one paragraph].
2. The facts, each with its source and date.
3. A line that begins "What I couldn't verify:" and lists anything I should treat as unconfirmed.
4. Links.

## Rules
- Never attach a claim to a source that didn't make it.
- No "experts say" or "studies show" without a name.
- If you can't find it, say you can't find it.

title: Fact-check pass
text:
# Skill: Fact-check pass
This skill serves [your name]. Run it on any draft that contains a number, a name, a date, or a quote, before I send or publish it.

## Check every one of these
1. Numbers: each has a source and a date in the text or in a note. Flag any that don't.
2. Names and titles: current, spelled right. Flag any you can't confirm.
3. Dates: correct, and consistent with each other.
4. Quotes: real, attributed, under [15] words, one per source.
5. Claims about what someone "said" or "reported": the source actually says that.

## Output
A short list: [item], [status: confirmed / can't confirm / wrong], [what to change].
Then the draft with changes marked.

## Rules
- "Can't confirm" is a valid answer. Never upgrade it to "confirmed" to be helpful.
- Don't rewrite anything except the flagged items.

title: My posts
text:
# Skill: My posts
This skill serves [your name]. Use it when I ask for a post for [LinkedIn / wherever].

## What a post of mine is
- Opens on a specific fact, moment, or number, never on a question or a hook formula.
- Holds one opinion I'd defend in the comments.
- [Length: e.g., 120 to 200 words.] Uneven line lengths. Not one sentence per line for the whole post.
- Ends on the point, not on "Thoughts?"

## Never
- Hashtag walls. Emoji. Exclamation points.
- "I'm excited to announce." "Humbled." "Game-changer."
- [Anything I've caught it doing before]

## Always
- Draft, then I edit.
- If it's about my company, check it against my brand rules skill first.
